content.stem:
In the figure, \(D\) and \(E\) are points on the sides \(AB\) and \(AC\) of triangle \(ABC\) such that \(DE \parallel BC\). \(AD = 4\) cm, \(DB = 6\) cm and \(DE = 5\) cm.

(i) Show that \(\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC\).

(ii) Find the length of \(BC\).

(iii) Find the ratio of the area of \(\triangle ADE\) to the area of the trapezium \(DBCE\).

diagrams.alt: Triangle ABC with A at the top, B at the bottom left and C at the bottom right; BC is horizontal. D is a point on AB and E is a point on AC, and the segment DE is drawn parallel to BC. AD is labelled 4 cm, DB is labelled 6 cm and DE is labelled 5 cm. BC is not labelled.
diagrams.solutionAlt: In step 1 the common angle at A and the equal corresponding angles ADE and ABC are marked. In step 4 the trapezium DBCE is shaded.

hints: Since \(DE \parallel BC\), look for pairs of corresponding angles.
The ratio of areas of similar triangles is the square of the ratio of corresponding sides. What is \(AD : AB\)?

solution.modelAnswer:
(i) In \(\triangle ADE\) and \(\triangle ABC\): \(\angle A\) is common and \(\angle ADE = \angle ABC\) (corresponding angles, \(DE \parallel BC\)). So \(\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC\) (AA).

(ii) \(\frac{DE}{BC} = \frac{AD}{AB} = \frac{4}{10}\), so \(BC = \frac{5 \times 10}{4} = 12.5\) cm.

(iii) \(\frac{\text{ar}(\triangle ADE)}{\text{ar}(\triangle ABC)} = \left(\frac{4}{10}\right)^2 = \frac{4}{25}\). Trapezium \(DBCE = 25 - 4 = 21\) parts, so the required ratio is \(4 : 21\).

steps.title: Prove the triangles similar
steps.expression: \angle DAE = \angle BAC,\quad \angle ADE = \angle ABC \;\Rightarrow\; \triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC
steps.explanation: \(\angle A\) is common to both triangles. Because \(DE \parallel BC\) and \(AB\) is a transversal, \(\angle ADE = \angle ABC\) (corresponding angles). Two pairs of equal angles give similarity.

steps.title: Ratio of corresponding sides
steps.explanation: In similar triangles, corresponding sides are proportional. \(AD\) corresponds to \(AB\), and \(DE\) corresponds to \(BC\).

steps.title: Ratio of areas
steps.explanation: Take \(\text{ar}(\triangle ADE) = 4k\) and \(\text{ar}(\triangle ABC) = 25k\). The trapezium \(DBCE\) is what remains: \(25k - 4k = 21k\).
steps.rule: Areas of similar triangles are in the ratio of the squares of corresponding sides.

commonMistakes: Using \(\frac{AD}{DB} = \frac{DE}{BC}\), which gives \(BC = 7.5\) cm; \(DE\) corresponds to \(BC\) only through the whole sides \(AD\) and \(AB\).
Giving the ratio of areas as \(4 : 10\) or \(2 : 5\) (forgetting to square).
Answering \(4 : 25\) for part (iii), which compares \(\triangle ADE\) with the whole triangle instead of the trapezium.

alternativeMethods.title: Using DE and BC
alternativeMethods.description: Once \(BC = 12.5\) cm is known, the area ratio can also be found as \(\left(\frac{DE}{BC}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{5}{12.5}\right)^2 = \frac{4}{25}\).

rubric.notes: Part (i) needs two pairs of equal angles with reasons for the mark.

criteria.description: Proves the triangles similar with reasons
criteria.expectedEvidence: ∠A common; ∠ADE = ∠ABC (corresponding angles, DE ∥ BC); hence similar by AA
acceptedAlternatives: Basic proportionality theorem followed by SAS similarity
commonErrors: States 'DE ∥ BC so the triangles are similar' with no angle pairs

criteria.description: Squares the ratio of sides for the areas
criteria.partialCreditRules: Follow-through from an incorrect BC if the squaring is correct.

criteria.description: Correct ratio of triangle ADE to trapezium DBCE

questions.authorNotes: Diagram is to scale: B(0, 0), C(12.5, 0), A(3, √91) so that AB = 10; D and E divide AB and AC in the ratio 2 : 3 from A, giving DE = 5 exactly. AC is not given in the question and is not needed.

content.stem: A map is drawn to a scale of \(1 : 20\,000\). A rectangular park is shown on the map as a rectangle measuring 4.5 cm by 3 cm. Find the actual area of the park in square kilometres.

hints: First convert each side on the map to its actual length in kilometres. How many centimetres are there in 1 km?

solution.modelAnswer: 1 cm on the map represents 20 000 cm \(= 0.2\) km. Actual sides: \(4.5 \times 0.2 = 0.9\) km and \(3 \times 0.2 = 0.6\) km. Area \(= 0.9 \times 0.6 = 0.54\) km².

steps.title: Interpret the scale
steps.explanation: There are 100 000 cm in 1 km, so 1 cm on the map stands for 0.2 km on the ground.
steps.rule: Scale factor \(k = \frac{1}{20\,000}\); actual length \(= \text{map length} \div k\).

steps.title: Actual lengths
steps.explanation: Convert each side of the rectangle separately.

steps.title: Actual area
steps.explanation: Multiply the actual length by the actual breadth.

commonMistakes: Multiplying the map area \(13.5\) cm² by \(20\,000\) instead of \(20\,000^2\): areas scale by the square of the scale factor.
Unit slips: using 1 km \(= 1000\) cm or 10 000 cm, which gives an answer that is off by a power of 10.

alternativeMethods.title: Area scale factor
alternativeMethods.description: Map area \(= 4.5 \times 3 = 13.5\) cm². Area scale: 1 cm² represents \(0.2^2 = 0.04\) km². Actual area \(= 13.5 \times 0.04 = 0.54\) km².

criteria.description: Correctly converts using the scale (lengths, or area with the square of the scale)

acceptedAlternatives: 54 hectares only if also given as 0.54 km²
commonErrors: 0.000027 km² (map area multiplied by 20 000 instead of 20 000²)

questions.authorNotes: Tolerance is 0 because the answer is exact. 0.54 km² = 54 hectares, but the question asks for km².
